nh_round_pond.blurb: Round Pond is one of the busiest bouldering zones in Pawtuckaway State Park, where glacial erratics of granite are scattered through hardwood forest near the water. It has a deep spread of problems, from easy V0 slabs through the double digits, with a little of everything: faces, cracks, arêtes, slopers and crimps. The granite is coarse in places and can wear skin fast, so plan on rest days. Fall is the sweet spot; spring and early summer bring thick bugs, and weekends can be crowded until school resumes.
nh_round_pond.parking_note: Aim for the Horse Farm lot, reached by turning onto the short dirt Round Pond Road past the boat ramp. When it is full, do not spill over onto the paved road.
nh_round_pond.approach: From the Horse Farm lot, follow the dirt road on foot for just under a mile to the pond; the boulders sit along the left side as you arrive.

nh_02_tier_1_left_side_boulder_s.blurb: The largest cluster of boulders at Sundown, sitting left of the Boulder Loop Trail near the Albany Covered Bridge off the Kancamagus Highway. Problems here run from V0 to about V10, with the bulk in the V1 to V6 range, so there is plenty for a mixed group. Many boulders have flat landings and the walk in is short, which makes it a comfortable place to spend a family day. Some blocks are lightly traveled and may need a brush before climbing. The river is close to the lot, handy on warm days.
nh_02_tier_1_left_side_boulder_s.parking_note: Use the Boulder Loop Trail lot just south of the Albany Covered Bridge, off the Kancamagus Highway about six miles west of Conway. If the bridge is shut, leave the car on the highway side and walk across.

nh_waimea.blurb: Waimea is the steepest, most committing wall at Rumney, with a swooping, wave-shaped profile of overhanging schist. The climbing is powerful and technical, dominated by sport routes in the 5.11 to 5.14 range, with a handful of easier lines, a few trad routes and little in the way of warm-ups. It faces south and a bit west, so it soaks up afternoon sun, yet the steepness keeps many lines dry in the rain. Expect a long approach by sport-crag standards and bring your own quickdraws for projecting.
nh_waimea.parking_note: Leave your vehicle in the main Rumney lot rather than on the road shoulder, then continue on foot.
nh_waimea.approach: Follow the roadside path from the lot, climb the steep steps to the hillside trail, and angle uphill past the Bonsai wall to arrive at the right side of Waimea. It is a stiff half-hour climb.

nh_main_cliff_4.blurb: The centerpiece of Sundown Ledge in the eastern Kancamagus area, the Main Cliff is a steep wall with bolted and trad lines in roughly equal numbers. Most of the climbing sits in the 5.11 to 5.13 range, with a handful of moderates and a few aid lines. It tends to be quiet, even on busy weekends, which makes it a calm alternative to Rumney. Many first bolts are high above rocky ground, so a stick clip earns its weight. The walk in crosses a talus field.
nh_main_cliff_4.parking_note: Park by the Albany Covered Bridge, where Passaconaway Road meets the Kancamagus Highway, and cross the river on foot to reach the Boulder Loop Trail.

nh_humphrey_s_bouldering.blurb: A scatter of boulders below Humphrey's Ledge, west of North Conway, with problems from VB up to V9 and a good share in the V0 to V3 range. The ledge itself is known as a quieter alternative to the busier cliffs in the valley, and the boulders share that low-key feel. Expect a mix of cracks, caves and edges. Bring pads, and remember that roadside parking is allowed on only one side of the road.
nh_humphrey_s_bouldering.parking_note: From Route 302 follow West Side Road for roughly three miles; the ledge rises on your right. Pull off only on the cliff side of the road.

nh_rines_hill.blurb: Rines Hill is one of several small crags in the New Durham area east of Lake Winnipesaukee. The climbing is split between short trad routes, mostly easy to moderate (5.7 and 5.8 are the commonest grades), and boulder problems that run from V0 to V7, many of them on the easier end. A tall clean boulder near the cliff base is a highball for the brave. Routes here are short and good for beginners learning to place gear. Walk-ins use rough forest tracks, and cairns and tape mark the trail.
nh_rines_hill.parking_note: Take Route 28 in Alton near the Wolfeboro line to Rines Hill Road and pull off near the Knight's Pond gate, leaving the road clear.
nh_rines_hill.approach: Walk about 300 feet to the remains of an old wooden gate on the left, then follow cairns and flagging through the woods until the main cliff comes into view.
